verifications.claim: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) has 160 to 2,000 km altitude.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Low-Earth orbit exists between 160 kilometers (100 miles) and 2,000 kilometers (1,240 miles) above Earth's surface.' R6: 'LEO is considered to be under altitudes of 2000 km' R12: 'Satellites in LEO are positioned between 160 to 2,000 km above Earth' R13: 'Low Earth orbit refers to the area situated closest to the Earth, below GEO and MEO. Satellites in LEO are located at an altitude of less than 2,000 km'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly state the exact altitude range for LEO as 160-2000 km.

verifications.claim: Geostationary Orbit (GEO) is a circular orbit 35,786 km above Earth's equator.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Satellites in geostationary orbit (GEO) fly above Earth’s equator... at an altitude of 35 786 km' R7: '35,786 kilometers (22,236 miles) above the ground' R12: 'GEO satellites are positioned 35,786 km from Earth'
verifications.reasoning: References explicitly describe GEO as circular, equatorial, at exactly 35,786 km altitude.

verifications.claim: Geostationary Orbit (GEO) allows satellites to stay over the same spot.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Geostationary satellites are useful because they appear as a fixed point in the sky.' R6: 'makes GEO satellites appear ‘stationary’ over one fixed spot.' R7: 'it looks like it is stationary (not moving)' R8: 'making the satellite appear to hover over a single point on the Earth'
verifications.reasoning: All references confirm GEO satellites remain fixed over one spot due to matching Earth's rotation.

verifications.claim: Perigee/Periapsis is the point in an orbit closest to the body being orbited.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the pericentre... the distance to the focus takes the minimal value the pericentre' R6: 'the point closest is the perigee' R18: 'periapsis is that point at which the two objects are closest to each other' R20: 'the point farthest from Earth in an elliptical orbit is the apogee, and the point closest is the perigee'
verifications.reasoning: Direct definitions match exactly across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Apogee/Apoapsis is the point in an orbit farthest from the body being orbited.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'For the ellipse there is also an apocentre for which the distance to the focus takes the maximal value' R6: 'the point farthest from Earth... is the apogee' R18: 'The apoapsis is that point at which they are the farthest' R20: 'the point farthest from Earth in an elliptical orbit is the apogee'

verifications.claim: Polar Orbit is an orbit that passes over or near both poles.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Polar orbits are a type of low Earth orbit... travel around Earth from, roughly, one pole to the other' R8: 'Polar orbits... satellites to pass over or very near both poles' R12: 'A polar orbit is an orbit with an inclination close to 90°. ... passes over the poles'

verifications.claim: Sun-Synchronous Orbit is a nearly polar orbit that passes over any given spot on Earth's surface at the same local solar time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'Sun-synchronous orbit (SSO) is a particular kind of polar orbit... pass over the same spot on Earth at the same local time every day' R8: 'Sun-synchronous orbits... a satellite passes over any given point on the Earth's surface at approximately the same local solar time' R12: 'a sun-synchronous orbit (SSO) is an orbit that will always show the same pattern to the Sun... pass over the same spot... at the same Local Time'

verifications.claim: Gravity equation is F = G m1 m2 / r^2.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'F = Gm1m2/r^2' R3: 'F = G (m1 + m2) ≈ Gm1... Newton's law of gravitation states: ... proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance' R16: 'F equals GMm over r squared' R18: 'F = G * (m1 * m2) / r^2'

verifications.claim: Orbital velocity is the square root of the gravitational constant times the central mass divided by the radius.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Orbital Speed Formula: The orbital speed v of a body is found using v = sqrt(Gm2/r)' R16: 'v equals the square root of GM over r' R17: 'For orbital motion: ( v = sqrt{frac{GM}{r}} )'
verifications.reasoning: Exact formula for circular orbital velocity.

verifications.claim: Early astronomers believed in geocentric models where everything orbited the Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'From ancient times until the 16th and 17th centuries, the motions of the planets were believed to follow perfectly circular geocentric paths' R4: 'early models to consider the Earth as a stationary object, around which all of the universe revolves. This is called a geocentric model'

verifications.claim: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed a heliocentric (sun-centered) model.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'In 1543, Nicolaus Copernicus published a heliocentric model of the Solar System' R4: 'The new model that was proposed... was the heliocentric model... Helio means sun.' R14: 'The Copernican Revolution refers to the replacement of the geocentric (Earth-centered) model... with a heliocentric (Sun-centered) model... named after Nicolaus Copernicus'

verifications.claim: Johannes Kepler determined that orbits were elliptical (not perfectly circular).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'In 1609, Kepler published the first two of his three laws of planetary motion. The first law states: The orbit of every planet is an ellipse with the sun at a focus.'

verifications.claim: Isaac Newton later developed the physical laws explaining why objects orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Despite developing these laws from observations, Kepler was never able to develop a theory to explain these motions. Isaac Newton produced the first such theory based around the concept of gravity.'
verifications.reasoning: Newton explained Kepler's laws with gravity.
